title: Negative one is pluralised: -1 formats as "-1 Bytes" while 1 formats as "1 Byte"
function: humansize::ISizeFormatter::fmt (the body behind FormatSizeI::format_size_i; the impl_style feature is not enabled in the harness so the wrapper itself could not be called)
property: formatting -v is the same as formatting v with a leading '-' (singular/plural unit choice depends only on magnitude)
evidence: formatters.rs says 'Remove "s" from the scale if the size is 1.x' but the check f64_eq(ipart, 1.0) uses the signed integer part, so it never fires for -1.x. Same for -1 kB-scale values, e.g. -1000 long decimal gives "-1 Kilobytes" vs "1 Kilobyte". Negation symmetry is the natural contract of format_size_i, whose docs show 1_000_000 -> "1 MB" and -1_000_000 -> "-1 MB".
